case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Department of Children & Families v. A.L.
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed an abuse-or-neglect finding based on prenatal cocaine use, holding Title 9 requires competent proof of actual harm to the child or of imminent danger or substantial risk of harm.
key_cases.relevance: A.L. resulted in dismissal of the finding because the record lacked proof of harm or risk.
key_cases.quote: If an expectant mother's drug use causes actual harm to the physical, mental, or emotional condition of a newborn child, a finding of abuse or neglect is appropriate.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Department of Children & Families v. I.S.
key_cases.holding: The Court held that a Title 9 action must be dismissed when no abuse or neglect is proved, but that jurisdiction may continue where the Division also proceeds under Title 30 to secure needed services for the child.
key_cases.relevance: I.S. requires dismissal of the Title 9 case when the abuse-or-neglect allegation is not sustained.
key_cases.quote: when the Division brings its complaint also under the authority granted to it under Title 30, the court's jurisdiction may continue

key_cases.case_name: N.J. Department of Children & Families v. R.R.
key_cases.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
key_cases.holding: The court reversed a 'not established' finding as unsupported by the record and directed that the allegation be deemed 'unfounded' so the records would be treated accordingly.
key_cases.relevance: R.R. is the remedy a parent obtains when the agency's finding cannot be sustained.
key_cases.quote: As we find that the Division erred in finding the allegation was "not established," the Division shall deem the allegation to be "unfounded" and treat the records accordingly.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. C.H.
key_cases.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
key_cases.holding: The court held the trial judge's sua sponte dismissal of the abuse-or-neglect complaint mid-hearing violated due process and remanded, while affirming the dismissal that followed a noticed motion.
key_cases.relevance: C.H. sets the procedural conditions under which a dependency case may properly be dismissed.
key_cases.quote: the court's sua sponte dismissal of the abuse or neglect complaint against C.H. was a due process violation necessitating a remand
